records.rationale: All three ledger cases are delivered on main and each was reproduced by an independent verifier. S1 (route without spec fails; spec without route fails): vizra-core #18 made the contract test walk wildcard routes and fail closed on shapes it cannot map; the verifier's own mutations on the real router went red in both directions. S2 (generated client diff empty after regeneration) and N1 (hand-edited generated file rejected): vizra-user #12 re-vendored the contract at core 5f615d7 and added an exact six-operation test; the verifier re-vendored from core main with no diff and saw the drift check reject a hand edit. IMPLEMENTED, not VERIFIED: the ledger's evidence_required asks for CI job output of the both-direction drift failure on a deliberate mutation, and every red run so far is a verifier-local transcript. Known limits, recorded in docs/warroom/FOLLOWUPS.md: no CI compares vizra-user's vendored contract with core main; the worker's metrics mux is outside what the contract test walks.

acceptance.bullet: (VZ-FOUND-002) Route-without-spec and spec-without-route both fail CI (demonstrated)
(VZ-FOUND-002) Generated client diff is empty after regeneration
(VZ-FOUND-002) Hand-edited generated file is rejected by a drift check

records.rationale: Every ledger case is on vizra-core main and was reproduced by an independent verifier. S1 (`migrate up` from the release image on an empty DB): vizra-core #19 added a docker-build step that runs `vizra migrate` from the built runtime image against an empty, digest-pinned PostgreSQL twice and checks the ledger reads the head version, not dirty, both times; CI red on a deliberately broken migration (job 131221389383), green on the merged head (job 131223440387). R1 (dirty ledger reported, not auto-fixed): #19's integration test makes a real ledger dirty and asserts refusal with the version named and nothing repaired; red on a mutation (job 131217791460), green ordered and shuffled with no skips in build-test (run 43230273284). N1 (DROP COLUMN fails migrate-lint): vizra-core #18 made migrate-lint catch every column-drop spelling and never accept a file main's earlier script rejected, proven by a differential test; the #19 verifier re-ran the mutation on main. S2 (sqlc-verify passes) and N2 (editing sqlcgen output fails drift check): the #19 verifier ran `make ci` and an sqlcgen edit (exit 2) on the merged head; build-test runs both (`==> migrate-lint`, `==> sqlc-verify`). Outcome reading: no compatibility-window mechanism exists; migrate-lint rejects destructive statements in every up file unless a reviewed `-- allow-destructive:` marker sits on the line before, which the verifier judged a superset of rejecting inside a window. Recorded follow-up: a real window would need to refuse markers inside it.

acceptance.bullet: (VZ-FOUND-003) Hand-edited sqlc output fails drift check (demonstrated)
(VZ-FOUND-003) `migrate up` from the release image applies cleanly on empty DB
(VZ-FOUND-003) A DROP COLUMN in *.up.sql fails migrate-lint
(VZ-FOUND-003) Dirty migration ledger is detected and reported, not auto-fixed
